title: Power reduction during sustained high ambient operation
engineering_question: A vehicle intermittently reduces available power during sustained operation at high ambient temperature. What is happening and what evidence supports each hypothesis?
one_liner: Investigate intermittent thermal derating during high-load operation.
initial_input: Multiple design verification vehicles report a reduction in available drive power after approximately 40 to 55 minutes of sustained highway operation at ambient temperatures above 35 degC.
expected_impacted_domains: Thermal arbitration between cabin and battery loads
expected_reasoning_paths: TR-004 passes, so the arbitration implementation matches its specification - this eliminates an implementation defect and points at the specification
TR-003 fails specifically under concurrent cabin cooling demand, which is the discriminating condition
TR-041 is inconclusive and shows sensor error growing to 7 K under exactly the condition under investigation, so the measured temperature may understate the true hot cell
TR-005 passes but only at 25 degC coolant inlet, so it does not cover the failing condition
Cooling plate braze coverage FM-200 and FM-007 remain a live alternative hypothesis because TR-032 shows coverage problems on a related population
known_unknowns: No heat rejection measurement exists at elevated coolant inlet temperature
No cell temperature gradient mapping exists at elevated coolant inlet temperature
Sensor error band under sustained high load is not defined in any acceptance criterion
Refrigerant circuit capacity split between cabin and battery is not quantified in the environment
data_classification: SIMULATED ENTERPRISE ARTEFACT - not OEM, customer or proprietary data
